newsitem.title: GUAM: Moments before KAL crash were 'dreamlike'-survivor.
newsitem.headline: Moments before KAL crash were 'dreamlike'-survivor.

text.p: Two Korean men who miraculously survived the fiery crash of Korean Air Lines Flight 801 on Guam said on Thursday the moments surrounding impact were like a dream or a movie.
"The whole thing seemed to pass in not more than three minutes -- like a movie scene," Hong Hyun-suen told South Korea's KBS public television station.
In a videotaped bedside interview made available to Reuters, Hong, one of only 27 survivors of the 254 people on the doomed flight, sat upright and had no visible wounds.
"First there was smoke, then there were loud booms. When I got out of the wreck and looked up, the plane had completely disintegrated."

Shin Hyun, another Korean man who lived through the ordeal on Wednesday morning, said his memory went blank just after he heard the cabin crew instruct passengers to prepare to land at Guam's international airport.

"In what seemed like a dream, I then remember hearing people screaming for help, but I was in an almost hallucinogenic state and couldn't move or do much to help them," said Shin, from the southwestern Korean city of Kwangju.
Shin, whose face was swollen and cut but who spoke clearly, said: "I feel reasonably good, considering.
"I'm okay, but my heart is in great pain to hear the bad news about so many of the others," he said.
Doctors at Guam Memorial Hospital said they avoided telling the survivors of the fate of fellow passengers to avoid upsetting the patients.
Five other people were alive when they were pulled from the smouldering wreckage, but died later in hospital.
Eight other survivors, all suffering serious burns, were flown on Thursday on a U.S. military plane to the South Korean capital Seoul for transfer to burn centres, a U.S. official said.
